reason: The regolith needs its iron-bearing fraction separated before processing, but no separator is explicitly listed.
expectation: The compatibility list should reveal how to separate or prepare the feedstock.

effect: Screened regolith has no available partner yet, so a separator or other preparation must come first.
reaction: The empty compatibility list makes the missing preparation more apparent.
reason: Steel may be used to build the missing separation equipment, so its available partners should help identify the next step.
expectation: The compatibility list will show what can be constructed from the steel.

alternatives.reason: Checking the retort could reveal how to connect it, though the feedstock also needs separation.

effect: Steel and the power cable made the missing electromagnet, so the screened regolith can now be separated.
reaction: The switchable electromagnet is a satisfying, physically clear solution.
reason: The electromagnet should extract the magnetic iron-bearing fraction from the screened regolith.
expectation: The separator will produce an iron-bearing feedstock for the retort.

effect: The separator produced iron-rich concentrate, ready for the materials retort once it is connected.
reaction: The distinction between magnetic separation and identifying minerals by color is useful.
reason: The retort is explicitly described as unconnected beside the hydrogen outlet, so connecting it is the next practical step.
expectation: The retort will connect to the hydrogen supply for processing the concentrate.

effect: The retort is connected to hydrogen and heat, with its liner ready for the concentrate.
reaction: The contained exhaust and condensate make the setup feel more thought through.
reason: The iron-rich concentrate is ready to be processed in the hydrogen-fed retort.
expectation: Heating the concentrate with hydrogen will produce a usable iron-bearing product.

effect: The retort produced porous, weak iron sponge that needs further forming at the press.
reaction: The reduction explains why the metal is not yet a strong finished material.
reason: The result explicitly brings the protected carrier to the workshop press, making that the clear next step.
expectation: The press will consolidate the sponge into a more usable iron form.

effect: The heated press consolidated the iron into a dense billet; the new goal is to shape a process frame.
reaction: The distinction between consolidating the metal and shaping parts is useful.
reason: The billet needs a separate shaping operation, but the available result does not identify how to make the frame.
expectation: Its available partners should reveal how to shape it into the process frame.

alternatives.reason: The press might also shape the billet, but its prior use does not establish that.

effect: The press shaped the billet into iron bars and brackets suitable for non-pressure supports.
reaction: Using the press for both consolidation and shaping is straightforward.
reason: The fuel-fab footing provides the prepared site for the process frame, and the bars and brackets are its likely structural components.
expectation: The iron parts will form a process frame on the prepared footing.

effect: The bars and brackets completed the process frame on the prepared footing, finishing the chapter's goals.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the local feedstock become a practical support, with the precision vessel still distinguished from the locally made frame.

mostWorthwhile.text: Reducing the concentrate and consolidating the sponge made the route from mineral to useful metal understandable, including why reduction alone does not produce a strong part.

leastWorthwhile.text: Inspecting the screened regolith gave no actionable partners; it established that preparation was missing but did little to identify it.

surprise.text: The separator was made from steel and the power cable, and the explanation of a switched electromagnet made the initially missing equipment understandable.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly purposeless. The separator recipe was not obvious from the initial object names, but its construction was explained once discovered.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see how the locally made frame supports the return-fuel installation; the chapter's physical explanations made that next stage interesting.
